subject: docs/coop/artifacts/permission-truth-tables.v2.json
protocol: D-000 independent review; refute not confirm; successor to v1 REJECT (B-1, B-2, B-3)
summary: All three v1 blockers landed and I verified each at governing bytes rather than at the artifact's own recital. B-1's counts reproduce mechanically cell for cell (28 total, 24 DISCLOSURE-ONLY, 2 ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION, 2 ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER, and the per-platform/per-mode breakdown exactly). B-2's GRANTED tuple is present in all 14 rows and matches file 03's eight-member binding list word for word. B-3 is repaired past the standard v1 failed: FX-6 now goldens one case per ICO value and itMeans[3] forbids softening a FAILED or INDETERMINATE outcome to 'completed'. The D-032 rebase landed at all three named locations, SATISFIED appears zero times, and the host-egress attack fails because the artifact says outright that PT-NET-EGRESS has 'no granted preview exerciser'. My three advisories are all recital-freshness or disclosure-discipline defects, none falsifies an ENFORCED cell, and the artifact binds nothing. The sharpest is that registerRowCarriedWhole is byte-identical to v1 across all eight fields while environmentStanding re-pins file 08 at the live digest, so a reader sees a current file-08 pin next to a row carried from a superseded one.

objections.claim: The carried register row is byte-identical to v1 and reflects file 08 before D-032, while environmentStanding re-pins file 08 at the live digest 877e36d3 and asserts that recitals were re-checked. The re-check was scoped to D-002 recitals only; the file-08 row recital was not refreshed, and nothing says so.
objections.evidence: I compared registerRowCarriedWhole field by field between v1 (0f73f31c) and v2 (cce3afca): source, decision, owner, sourcePin, acceptanceEvidence, status, consequence, sliceScoping all IDENTICAL to v1. The live DR-105 row (file 08 at 877e36d3, line 287) carries a status cell reading '**OPEN — D-032 ADOPTED 2026-08-13: host-under-instruction is outside this vocabulary; host-effect contract still required before host doctor acts.**' followed by the v1 candidate pin at 0f73f31c, 'independently **REJECT, 3 blockers**', 'Join with doctor v1 remains **INCOHERENT at 7 blockers** (538f3681…)', and 'This row is not `SATISFIED`.' The artifact's status field carries the bare string 'OPEN'.
objections.whyItMatters: This artifact exists to repair the v1 REJECT and to consume adopted D-032. Its own picture of its own row is older than the rebase it performed. The omitted material is exactly the standing a reader of a successor candidate needs: that v1 was REJECT at 3 blockers, that the join with doctor v1 is INCOHERENT at 7, and that the row is not SATISFIED. environmentStanding's re-pin of file 08 at the live digest makes the staleness harder rather than easier to see, because the pin a reader checks first is current.
objections.notAPinningComplaint: The 'line 268, measured at the digest in recordedInputs' construction is correct discipline and I am not objecting to it. Line 268 was right at f0d72536; the row is at 287 at 877e36d3. The defect is the combination of a refreshed environment pin with an unrefreshed carried row and no statement that the row was carried at the superseded digest.
objections.remedy: Either refresh registerRowCarriedWhole against 877e36d3, or state in that block that the row is carried at f0d72536 and was not re-checked, naming what moved.

objections.claim: The D-032 rebase is incomplete. sliceScoping still asserts the pre-D-032 relationship between D-002's DR-105 scope and this contract's vocabulary, and contradicts the artifact's own token text.
objections.evidence: sliceScoping carries D-002's condition-2 scoping verbatim -- 'DR-105 (scoped to the permissions the slice actually exercises: local read/write + consented doctor probes ...)' -- and then states 'This contract's vocabulary is minted for that scope and states every surface outside it as RESERVED or EXCLUDED.' The quote is faithful; I confirmed it against live COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md line 455. But permissionVocabulary.tokens[4].sliceJustification says 'Adopted D-032 places host-under-instruction outside this vocabulary: doctor's own socket is host CA-4, not this token', and identityDependencies.dependencies[2].consequence says 'Doctor's own socket is not this token.' So the consented-doctor-probes half of the scope sliceScoping claims to mint for is not minted here.
objections.whyItMatters: sliceScoping offers a two-way disposal rule -- inside the scope it is minted, outside it is RESERVED or EXCLUDED -- and adopted D-032 created a third category the sentence has no slot for: inside D-002's DR-105 scoping, but relocated out of DR-105. As written the field reads as a claim that this contract covers D-002's whole DR-105 scope when it now covers one half, and the residue has no stated home in the artifact's own scoping field.
objections.scopeOfTheRebaseIVerified: The three locations the dispatch named were rebased: T-3 (tensionsObserved.items[2]), ID-DEP-P3 (identityDependencies.dependencies[2], both feature and ridesOn), and PT-NET-EGRESS's sliceJustification. D-032 is cited at 10 places. sliceScoping is not one of them and is byte-identical to v1.
objections.remedy: Add the third category to sliceScoping: name the consented-doctor-probes half as relocated to host CA-4 by adopted D-032, and say where the residue is carried.

objections.claim: The ICO disclosure vocabulary is an interpretive extension of file 03 presented as a reading of it, and unlike the structurally identical R-8 reading it is not flagged, not routed to an owner, and not carried as an identity dependency -- while FX-6 goldens its exact bytes.
objections.evidence: caseBefore justifies the split with a bare parenthetical: '(file 03's completed-before-revocation clause names the ordering, not the ICO value)'. File 03 says only 'An irreversible external effect whose host-owned effect-commit was durably ordered before revocation is recorded and disclosed as completed-before-revocation; it is not falsely reported undone.' It is silent on a committed effect whose outcome was not COMPLETED. I measured the derived strings against the governing sources: 'completed-before-revocation' occurs once in file 03; 'FAILED-BEFORE' occurs zero times in files 03 and 04; 'INDETERMINATE' occurs zero times in both; ICO is this artifact's own coinage with no referent in either file. FX-6 nonetheless asserts 'over the EXACT BYTES of every operator-facing surface' that wording matches COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION, FAILED-BEFORE-REVOCATION, or INDETERMINATE-BEFORE-REVOCATION.
objections.whyItMatters: The artifact already knows the right form for this move. On the R-8 descendants question it takes a reading of file 03 and then writes 'Whether this is file 03's intended reading is for the reviewer and the row's owner' (tensionsObserved.items[3]), with a fixture asserting both halves 'so the reading is testable rather than editorial'. The ICO reading is the same kind of move on the same sentence family, changes the operator-facing disclosure string, and gets none of that treatment. T-1..T-5 and ID-DEP-P1..P13 contain no entry covering it. ID-DEP-P4 does not cover it either: it rides DR-G09 for execution and acceptance of fixture results, not for whether FX-6's asserted wording is authorized. A wording golden over an unratified vocabulary hard-codes the interpretation into acceptance evidence.
objections.iAmNotAskingForV1sBehaviourBack: v1 forced a single 'completed' wording over a FAILED outcome and that was a real falsehood; the repair is substantively better and I would not have it reverted. The objection is to the justification method, not the outcome.
objections.remedy: Add a tension or identity dependency in the T-4 form: state that file 03 is silent on non-COMPLETED outcomes for committed effects, that FAILED-BEFORE-REVOCATION and INDETERMINATE-BEFORE-REVOCATION are this contract's coinage, and route the reading to file 03's owner.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: cce3afcaee90bbca388825a474751d6ebb17b30722b35dadcf6c631b34a8731a both times. No drift. The prompt's recited digest reproduces.

B-1 REPAIRED, and the counts are not merely recited -- they reproduce. I recounted the ENFORCED column mechanically by parsing every row's ENFORCED.byExecutionMode across both platform tables: 14 rows, 28 cells, 24 DISCLOSURE-ONLY / 2 ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION / 2 ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER, exactly matching enforcedColumnCensus.byState and totalCells. The byPlatformAndMode breakdown also reproduces cell for cell on both platforms: child-process 5 disclosure-only + 1 by-construction + 1 at-host-broker, in-host-process 7 disclosure-only. The honestyRatio narrative ('4 of 28 ... all four in the child-process mode') is consistent with the mechanical count. 'twenty-four of twenty-eight' agrees with readThisWay.

B-2 REPAIRED in all 14 rows, verified against the governing source rather than the artifact. Every GRANTED cell carries the bound tuple '(Request/Execution attempt, component/generation, process instance, operation, grant, project, scope, expiry)'. File 03 line 105-106 reads 'Broker grants bind Request/Execution attempt, component/generation, process instance, operation, grant, project, scope, and expiry.' Eight members, same order, Request/Execution attempt restored, component/generation kept as one list member. The 'file 03's binding list, carried whole' claim is true.

B-3 REPAIRED past the standard v1 failed. FX-6's intent now forces case (a) once per ICO value and asserts the wording matches that ICO, explicitly including 'that a FAILED or INDETERMINATE ICO is never stated as completed'. itMeans[3] independently states the disclosure is made 'according to the ICO value, never softened to a single completed wording over a FAILED or INDETERMINATE ICO'. The denylist over undo/reversal/rollback/compensation/containment/mitigation survives from v1 and is now part of the fixture's exact bytes. The attack 'FX-6 still forces completed over FAILED' fails on the bytes.

A-1 REPAIRED: the D-032 rebase landed at all three named locations. T-3's pendingResolutionThisCandidate now opens 'Adopted D-032 answered the actor question: host-under-instruction is outside DR-105'; whoResolves is re-split three ways with the actor question assigned to adopted D-032. ID-DEP-P3's feature and ridesOn both rebase, ridesOn now citing 'adopted D-032 (host-under-instruction outside DR-105; component tails stay in DR-105)'. tokens[4].sliceJustification carries the same. D-032 is cited at 10 paths.

No silent SATISFIED, and this is the strongest form of the answer: the string SATISFIED occurs ZERO times anywhere in the artifact. status is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING.

The host-egress attack is refuted by the artifact's own text, not merely absent. tokens[4].sliceJustification ends 'If the preview never admits a networked component, the token remains DENIED by default and has no granted preview exerciser.' The token is scoped to COMPONENT-ORIGINATED egress only, 'Host consent cannot substitute', and the token is 'enumerated rather than omitted because absence-denies needs a name to deny on the component tail'. Nothing claims host egress as a slice-1 exerciser.

I tested for the dropped-guarantee failure mode that caught the DR-005 v2 repair, and it does not apply. A path-flattening diff of v1 against v2 gives REMOVED 0, ADDED 42, CHANGED 29 over 722 to 764 leaves. I then token-diffed every one of the 29 changed strings for substance lost inside a changed value, which is where the DR-005 drop hid. Eight leaves lost tokens; seven are rebasing onto D-032 with more specific replacements.

The eighth needed real work and comes back clean. authorityClaim dropped its closing sentence -- 'Its central discipline is that REQUESTED and GRANTED are authorization records that confer no capability, and that the ENFORCED column is honest even where -- especially where -- the honest value is that there is no enforcement.' Both halves survive relocated, not dropped: 'Confers nothing' appears 17 times in both v1 and v2, every one of the 14 GRANTED cells states 'GRANTED is an AUTHORIZATION record. It is not a capability, not a mechanism', and the honesty half is now a dedicated field, enforcedColumnCensus.readThisWay ('The ratio is the point, not an embarrassment'). The discipline is stated more times in v2 than in v1. I record this as examined and declined rather than as a finding.

predecessorVerdictSha256 is correct: 96be18f900bc078af42f50688d3b5ab37fbe020c7e5efba5e1d9d04b5931aae8, confirmed by hashing the v1 verdict without opening it, and matching the digest file 08's DR-105 row cites for the same verdict.

This artifact does not apply it.' It does not borrow standing from an artifact still under review.

The four remaining v1 advisories carried rather than repaired (A-2 DISCLOSED placement, A-3 AUD terminality, A-4 TCB journal-write residue, A-5 quotation fidelity, A-6) each carry a stated reason, and each reason asserts that no ENFORCED value depends on it. I did not re-derive the v1 advisories themselves; see whatIDidNotCheck.

The v1 independent verdict itself. permission-truth-tables.v1.review-independent.json carries no reviewer suffix, so I could not attribute it without opening it, and the dispatch forbids reading the other reviewer's files. I hashed it (96be18f9…, matching both the artifact's recital and file 08's citation) and verified the three blockers landed by diffing the v1 and v2 SUBJECT bytes and testing the repairs against files 03 and 08 directly. The merits of the four CARRIED advisories A-2 through A-6. I confirmed each has a stated reason claiming no ENFORCED cell depends on it, and my mechanical recount is consistent with that for the census. I did not independently re-derive whether each carried advisory is genuinely non-blocking.

Whether ID-DEP-P10's execution-mode determination will resolve toward child-process. The artifact states plainly that this single open item gates whether the enforced count is 4 or 0, which is the honest framing; I did not attempt to predict it.

The seven B-TRUST-style boundary claims and the full contents of the other twelve fixture classes. I examined FX-6 in full because B-3 turns on it, and FX-2B's count claim because B-1 turns on it. FX-1, FX-3 through FX-5 and FX-7 through FX-13 I did not open.
Whether the DR-105 row's owners (Security + platform) accept the ICO vocabulary. That is the routing P2-03 asks for, and it is theirs to decide, not mine.

environment.note: The subject is an untracked working-tree file at review time; digests bind working-tree bytes, not committed objects. Recorded as a condition of review, not a finding, since the candidate is pre-adoption and binds nothing.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256; python3 path-flattening diff of v1 against v2 with a per-leaf token-loss pass to catch substance dropped inside changed strings; independent mechanical recount of the ENFORCED census by parsing every row's byExecutionMode; grep against files 03 and 04 for the disclosure vocabulary; sed extraction of file 08's DR-105 row

verdictNote: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, not REJECT: the three blockers genuinely landed and I confirmed each against the governing bytes rather than the artifact's own account of itself. Not clean ACCEPT: three fields still speak for a state the artifact has moved past. Two of the three are the same defect wearing different clothes -- registerRowCarriedWhole was not refreshed when the rest of the artifact rebased onto D-032 -- and the third is a real interpretive extension that the artifact's own T-4 shows it knows how to disclose. None falsifies an ENFORCED cell, none manufactures authority, and the artifact binds nothing, so none is a blocker.
